content: Back DAOR E&C Co., Ltd DAOR E&C Co., Korea is a company engaged in the production and construction of concrete structures: concrete bridges, large cable-stayed bridges, liquefied natural gas tanks, underground tunnels, and heavy lifting structures. Over 40 years of operation, the company has invented and implemented a huge number of unique developments. And now they are all publicly available. The published data contains more than 400 GB of internal company information, and it is very interesting information. All of the company's unique designs, some of which are commercial secrets. In addition, the published data includes plans and drawings for each of the company's hundreds of completed projects. Schematics of such projects as bridges, tunnels, and liquefied natural gas tanks are now publicly available—information that should be kept secret because it is of great interest to other countries. A report on what was found in these documents is already being prepared for Comrade Kim Jong-un. content: Back Inicio - Ganadería Revuelta Inicio - Ganadería Revuela, Mexico - the company produces beef. It has its own production chain, which includes: feedlots, slaughterhouse, packing factory and finished product factory. The company supplies meat to the United States, Canada, Japan and many other countries. The company claims to “offer a wide range of products in vacuum-packed packaging that guarantees hygiene and food safety.” However, things are so good only in the public field. A completely different story can be seen if one examines the company's internal reports. Over 600GB of internal company information, including sales reports, is publicly available. As the graphs show, Ganadería Revuela is doing very badly. Profits are falling every year. Because of this, the company starts to economize on the manufacture of its products, buys cheaper feed and does not check the quality so carefully anymore. More and more often they use low-quality additives and feed to accelerate the growth of cattle. Also, all financial documents and personal data of the company's employees and all customers became publicly available. Back welldone.com.tw Welldone Company is the first legal remittance company for migrant workers in Taiwan：
Approved by the Financial Supervisory Commission to conduct financial technology innovation experiments for migrant workers’remittances in 2018.
Obtained the first business license for migrant worker remittance business issued by the Financial Supervisory Commission in 2021, and renewed the license in 2024.

Their services cover Indonesia, Vietnam, Philippines and Thailand, providing legal, safe and fast remittance services for migrant workers 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

However, all personal information of over 700,000 customers was leaked.
This includes names, phone numbers, dates of birth, passwords, ROC Resident Certificates, and even selfies.
The release of all this information depends on Welldone's attitude.
If the company ignores this fact and refuses to discuss it, all information will be released, and then it will be necessary to engage with customers. content: Back Fullerton Surgical Center (FSC) Fullerton Surgical Center, USA, is a surgical clinic offering services in general surgery, orthopedics, otolaryngology, plastic surgery, pain management, urology, and gastroenterology. Of course, all these services cost a fortune, and the US healthcare system is disgusting, but that's not what we're talking about right now. Americans have written laws that make protecting patient information in healthcare a top priority, requiring strict compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (CMIA+HIPAA). This is not just a legal obligation, but also a critical element for patient trust and the quality of medical services. However, US clinics do a very poor job of complying with this law. A telling example is Fullerton Surgical Center. Most likely, they deliberately made their data protection critically poor because they insured against the risk of leakage and are now going to receive a big payout. At the same time, FSC is not interested in the safety of patients and the confidentiality of the personal data of people who trust them with their lives. As a result of the data leak, critically important information that allows the identification of every patient in the history of the medical institution became publicly available. The data contains names, dates of birth, complete medical histories, and other confidential information that is classified as medical confidentiality.  FSC failed to protect this information and now, along with millions in compensation, will face a collective lawsuit that will be much larger and could lead to the bankruptcy of the medical institution. content: Back www.wyongleagues.com.au Wyong Rugby League Club, Australia is a network of 12 organizations, each offering entertainment, recreational and dining opportunities and promoting membership of their club. It is the membership card that opens up a full range of entertainment for its holder. And these cards have become the company's weakest point. content: Back seabridge.eu+efico.com Seabridge, Belgium is a logistics service center and distribution platform for green coffee. They buy coffee from other countries and bring it to Europe. The company says it operates to green eco-standards and also “acts as an example of work for the whole community.” The company has a special focus on cybersecurity. They are proud of their security system, which is impossible to hack. Well...there's no need to comment here, we say hello to the very well-paid cybersecurity expert Youri Segers. Because of the published data, anyone can now see the other side of this business - fraud against suppliers, overpriced sales and total control of their employees. Anyone can compare documents on green coffee purchases in the producing countries and then look at the price at which it is sold in Belgium. And then one can also remember how much coffee costs at the nearest coffeeshop. Of course, the published archive contains a complete list of all employees of the company, as well as personal data of the employees. In addition - there is an interesting document about what employees are forbidden and what they are allowed to do. There are some surprising facts in this document. For example, employees are strictly forbidden to join any Internet discussions, view pornography, as well as - download any audio-visual files. At any time, the company can block any of the sites, as well as - to take devices “to check”. The company reserves the right to read emails and correspondence, as well as to examine and copy any date. Allegedly, this is done to ensure security. Again, no comment. content: Back Spohn + Burkhardt GmbH & Co KG At Spohn + Burkhardt, Germany produce custom control transmitters, control systems and resistors that are robust and comfortable. These are highly customized and complex products that are often designed and manufactured in a single piece. On the other hand, control panels for industrial and agricultural machinery can be produced in hundreds or even thousands of units. At Spohn + Burkhardt has been developing unique solutions for many years to become one of the few manufacturers of this unique equipment. The company's inventions and unique designs are protected by patents and copyright law. But now anyone can use all these designs for their own purposes. Of course, the publication of this complete data archive jeopardizes the existence of the company, because now customers do not need to contact them directly - cheaper and possibly better quality analogs will soon appear. The Turk Hack Team, a group of notorious hackers, claimed responsibility for the attack, which caused a major outage on the bank's website. This incident highlighted the vulnerability of even highly secured institutions to cyber threats. The motives for the attack included dominance, personal gain, personal satisfaction, and revenge. The Turk Hack Team's tactics involved an external denial of service, targeting the bank's website and disrupting its accessibility. The attack on the Central Bank of Malta's website resulted in a major outage, preventing users from accessing the site and potentially causing significant disruption to the bank's operations and services. The Turk Hack Team publicized their involvement in the attack through a post on Twitter, where they shared screenshots of the struggling website as it faltered under the weight of their assault. The attack on the Central Bank of Malta's website violated the availability aspect of the CIA Triad, compromising the bank's ability to provide uninterrupted access to its online services. Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, like the one employed in this incident, involve overwhelming a target system with traffic from multiple sources, making it difficult for legitimate users to access the site. In this case, the Turk Hack Team likely utilized a network of compromised computers, often referred to as a botnet, to inundate the bank's servers with requests, causing the website to slow down or become completely unresponsive. This tactic is a common tool used by cyber attackers to disrupt organizations and make a statement. While the full extent of the damage caused by the attack is not yet clear, it has raised important questions about the resilience of critical infrastructure in the face of cyber threats. Cyber Incident Victim: Ministry of the Russian Far East Development Date: Dec. 25, 2015 Location: Turkey Summary The Turk Hack Team (THT), a group of Turkish hackers, launched a series of cyber attacks on Russian and Iranian websites following the downing of a Russian fighter jet by the Turkish air force near the Syrian-Turkish border. THT defaced websites with anti-Putin messages, leaked personal data of Russian citizens, and conducted DDoS attacks on government ministry websites of both countries, including Russia's Ministry of the Far East Development and Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. CIA Posture Motives Tactics, Techniques & Procedures Confidentiality Integrity Availibility Personal Satisfaction Ideology Notoriety Personal Gain External Denial of Service (CISSM) Message Manipulation (CISSM) Exfiltration from Application Server (CISSM) Exfiltration from End Host (CISSM) Exfiltration from Network Infrastructure (CISSM) Threat Actor Type Location Turk Hack Team Hacker Turkey Description The Russian Federation and the Islamic Republic of Iran experienced a series of cyber attacks perpetrated by a group of Turkish hackers known as the Turk Hack Team (THT) in retaliation for the downing of a Russian fighter jet by the Turkish Air Force in November 2015. This incident sparked a wave of cyber aggression from THT, targeting both Russian and Iranian government websites and private citizen data. On December 25, 2015, THT initiated their campaign with a wave of website defacements, leaving anti-Putin messages on compromised sites. The group claimed to have defaced over 2000 websites, a bold statement of their hacking capabilities and a show of force. The messages denounced Putin, accusing him of treason and predicting his eventual downfall at the hands of the Russian people. Not content with mere defacement, THT sought to inflict further damage by breaching the personal information of Russian citizens. On December 26, 2015, they leaked the personal details of hundreds of individuals, including names, cities, phone numbers, emails, and even encrypted passwords harvested from online shopping sites. Accompanying this breach was a threat to continue their attacks, specifically targeting shopping site owners and companies. The third and final wave of attacks, executed on January 2, 2016, saw a shift in tactics as THT employed Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks to disrupt top Russian and Iranian government ministry websites. This rendered the sites inaccessible to legitimate users, effectively crippling their online presence. The targeted Russian ministries included critical departments such as the Ministry of the Russian Far East Development, the Ministry of Construction, and the State Atomic Energy Corporation ROSATOM. Meanwhile, Iran's Ministry of Information, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Energy, and the official website of the President of the Islamic Republic of Iran also fell victim to the onslaught. The attacks by THT showcased a well-coordinated and multi-faceted campaign, exploiting a variety of techniques to deface websites, steal and expose sensitive data, and disrupt government services. The group's actions caused significant disruption and raised tensions between the affected nations, highlighting the potential for cyber conflicts to escalate rapidly in today's interconnected world. THT's motivation was clear and politically driven, fueled by the desire to defend their nation's interests and retaliate against what they perceived as an act of aggression. Their methods, however, crossed legal and ethical boundaries, as they violated the privacy and security of innocent citizens and disrupted critical government infrastructure. The impact of these attacks underscores the importance of robust cyber defenses and the need for international cooperation to deter and respond to such incidents effectively. The group's history reveals a pattern of politically motivated hacking, having previously targeted the Vatican City's official website in response to Pope Francis' remarks on the Armenian genocide. THT's strong nationalist sentiments and support for Turkey's prime minister, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, guide their choice of targets and the timing of their attacks. The exposure of Russian citizens' personal information and the disruption caused to government ministries highlight the potential consequences of cyber attacks, which can range from privacy violations to significant operational disruptions. The incident serves as a stark reminder of the vulnerability of critical infrastructure and the need for proactive security measures to safeguard against such threats. The THT's campaign against Russia and Iran demonstrated a sophisticated and organized approach, causing concern among cybersecurity experts and government officials alike. The group's ability to deface websites, steal data, and execute DDoS attacks underscored their technical prowess and determination to cause disruption. This incident highlights the evolving nature of cyber threats and the challenges faced by nations in protecting their digital assets and critical infrastructure. The impact of THT's attacks extended beyond the temporary disruption of websites; it undermined trust in the security of personal information and government services. Recovering from such incidents can be a complex and lengthy process, requiring thorough investigations and the implementation of enhanced security measures to prevent similar attacks in the future. The affected Russian and Iranian ministries would need to conduct comprehensive assessments to identify vulnerabilities exploited by THT and bolster their defenses against future cyber aggression. In the aftermath of these attacks, international cooperation and information sharing become vital to understanding the tactics, techniques, and procedures employed by THT. By analyzing the group's methods and motivations, cybersecurity professionals can develop more effective strategies to mitigate the impact of future attacks and enhance the overall resilience of critical infrastructure worldwide. The incident also underscores the importance of public-private partnerships in cybersecurity, as collaboration between governments and private sector entities is crucial for defending against sophisticated cyber threats. The Turk Hack Team's cyber attacks against Russia and Iran stand as a testament to the evolving nature of cyber conflicts and the far-reaching impact they can have. Through a combination of website defacements, data breaches, and DDoS attacks, THT successfully disrupted government operations and exposed sensitive data, highlighting the persistent threat posed by politically motivated hacking groups. This incident serves as a critical case study in the ongoing battle for control and security in the digital domain. With its headquarters in Moscow, Russia, ROSATOM is a state corporation established in 2007 to consolidate all of the country's civil and defense-related nuclear industries. The organization oversees a wide range of activities, including the development of nuclear power plants, nuclear fuel production, and the management of radioactive waste. One of its key responsibilities is to represent the Russian Federation on the global stage in matters pertaining to the peaceful use of atomic energy, as well as ensuring the safe and secure operation of nuclear facilities within Russia. ROSATOM has become a significant player in the international nuclear market, offering its expertise and services to countries seeking to develop their own nuclear energy programs. ROSATOM's history can be traced back to the Soviet era, when the country was at the forefront of nuclear research and development. Over the years, Russia has made significant contributions to nuclear science and technology, and ROSATOM has played a pivotal role in harnessing this expertise for both domestic and international applications. The organization has a strong focus on innovation and has been instrumental in developing advanced nuclear reactor designs, including fast neutron reactors and small modular reactors. As the regulatory body, ROSATOM is committed to ensuring the highest standards of safety and security across Russia's nuclear industry. It works closely with international organizations and adheres to global best practices to maintain the integrity of its operations. ROSATOM has also prioritized sustainability and environmental responsibility, investing in research and development to minimize the environmental impact of nuclear energy production. In addition to its domestic responsibilities, ROSATOM has actively pursued international cooperation and collaboration. The organization has established itself as a trusted partner for countries seeking to develop nuclear energy programs, offering a range of services that include reactor design, construction, and fuel supply. ROSATOM has signed intergovernmental agreements with various countries, providing a framework for cooperation and ensuring the safe and secure transfer of technology. As a global leader in nuclear energy, ROSATOM has also taken on a role in promoting the peaceful use of atomic energy. The organization actively engages with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and other international forums to share its expertise and contribute to the development of global standards and best practices. ROSATOM's presence on the world stage underscores Russia's commitment to responsible nuclear energy development and its willingness to collaborate with the international community.                     , Armenian National Security Service Primary URL Location Industry https://www.nss.am/en Armenia Government - National Profile The National Security Service of Armenia, also known as the NSS Armenia or the Armenian National Security Service, is the primary intelligence agency of Armenia. With its headquarters in Yerevan, the NSS is tasked with ensuring the country's national security and safeguarding its interests. As a government entity, it operates under the direction of the Prime Minister, who oversees its activities and ensures its accountability. The NSS has a broad mandate, which includes counterintelligence, counter-terrorism, border security, and the protection of constitutional order and citizens' rights. It plays a critical role in maintaining the stability and security of Armenia, particularly in the context of regional conflicts and cyber threats. The organisation has been at the forefront of Armenia's efforts to counter cyberattacks and cyber espionage, as evidenced by its involvement in incidents such as the 2016 cyber war with Azerbaijan. In recent years, the NSS has also focused on strengthening its international cooperation, collaborating with foreign partners to enhance Armenia's security posture and contribute to global efforts against transnational threats. The organisation's website, nss.am, provides a public interface for Armenian citizens and international stakeholders to access information about the NSS's activities, initiatives, and relevant news updates. Through this online presence, the NSS strives for transparency and engagement with the communities it serves and protects. As Armenia continues to navigate complex geopolitical dynamics and evolving security challenges, the National Security Service remains a pivotal institution, dedicated to protecting the nation's sovereignty and the well-being of its citizens. The organisation's expertise and dedication are instrumental in safeguarding Armenia's interests and contributing to regional stability. Incidents Date Location Summary Sept. 2, 2016 Armenia Azerbaijani hacktivists, self-styled as the 'Anti-Armenia Team', breached Armenian government servers and leaked sensitive information, including passport details of foreign visitors and internal security reports. The incident highlights the ongoing cyber-conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan, two countries with a history of tense relations and military conflict over the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region. Experts suggest an insider may have been involved in the leak, rather than a direct hack as claimed by the hacktivists. April 1, 2016 Armenia The Nagorno-Karabakh conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan escalated into a cyber war involving hackers from both countries. The Turkish hacker group Turk Hack Team (THT) launched cyberattacks on Armenian servers, targeting various government and economic sectors. In response, the Armenian hacker group Monte Melkonian Cyber Army (MMCA) conducted counter-attacks on Azerbaijani government servers. The cyberwar resulted in the defacement and disruption of multiple websites, with both groups leveraging their technical capabilities to support their respective nations.

                    , Crédit Agricole Primary URL Location Industry https://www.credit-agricole.com France Financial Services Profile Crédit Agricole: A Global Banking Leader with a Rich History Crédit Agricole is a French multinational banking group that has been a cornerstone of the global financial industry for over 120 years. With its roots in agriculture and a strong commitment to serving the needs of local communities, Crédit Agricole has evolved into a leading financial services provider with a presence in over 47 countries. History Crédit Agricole was founded in 1870 as a mutual agricultural bank in France, with the aim of providing financial support to farmers and rural communities. Over the years, the bank expanded its operations and services, gradually transforming into a full-fledged commercial bank. In the 20th century, Crédit Agricole underwent significant modernization and internationalization, establishing subsidiaries and partnerships around the world. Business Activities Today, Crédit Agricole is a global banking leader, offering a wide range of financial services to individuals, businesses, and institutions. Its activities include: * Retail banking: providing personal banking services, credit cards, and mortgages to individuals * Corporate and investment banking: offering financial solutions to businesses, including mergers and acquisitions, capital markets, and transaction banking * Asset management: managing investments for institutional and individual clients * Insurance: providing life and non-life insurance products to individuals and businesses International Presence Crédit Agricole has a significant presence in Europe, with operations in over 20 countries, including France, Italy, Spain, and Poland. The bank also has a strong presence in the Americas, Asia, and Africa, with subsidiaries and partnerships in countries such as the United States, Brazil, China, and Egypt. Innovation and Sustainability Crédit Agricole is committed to innovation and sustainability, investing heavily in digital transformation and environmental initiatives. The bank has launched several digital platforms and mobile apps to enhance customer experience and improve access to financial services. Additionally, Crédit Agricole has set ambitious targets to reduce its carbon footprint and support sustainable development projects around the world. Cybersecurity As a leading financial institution, Crédit Agricole is a prime target for cyber threats. The bank has invested heavily in cybersecurity measures to protect its customers' data and prevent cyber attacks. Despite this, Crédit Agricole has been the victim of several high-profile cyber attacks in recent years, including a 2024 incident in which its website and mobile app were paralyzed by a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack. Conclusion Crédit Agricole is a global banking leader with a rich history, a strong commitment to innovation and sustainability, and a significant presence in over 47 countries. While the bank faces challenges in the rapidly evolving financial landscape, its dedication to serving the needs of its customers and communities has earned it a reputation as a trusted and reliable financial partner. Incidents Date Location Summary Feb. 7, 2024 France Crédit Agricole's website and mobile application were paralyzed for several hours due to a cyberattack claimed by the Turk Hack Team, a nationalist Turkish group. The attack, likely a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS), aimed to disrupt access to the bank's online services. Despite the disruption, the bank assured that no customer data was compromised. The attack is believed to be motivated by ideological reasons, possibly in response to France's arms sales to Armenia. June 27, 2023 Ukraine Credit Agricole Bank was targeted by the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) in a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack. The attack was part of a larger campaign against Ukrainian banks, aimed at disrupting online banking infrastructure. The group claimed to have knocked several bank websites offline and targeted authorization services, login portals, and loan processing systems. The attack was motivated by ideology, with the group opposing Ukraine's plans to become a cashless society.
